data.content_ref: inline:The argument collapses into the very induction Popper rejected because 'verisimilitude' cannot be operationalized without assuming the uniformity of nature. While the target claims the preference is merely a 'decision rule' based on past performance, the rationality of acting on this rule presupposes that a theory which survived past tests is more likely to survive future ones or describe reality accurately. Without this inductive bridge, the preference for the 'better-corroborated' theory is arbitrary; one could just as rationally prefer the worst-corroborated theory if no link between past survival and future reliability (truth-likeness) is assumed. Thus, invoking verisimilitude smuggles in the expectation that the future will resemble the past, violating Popper's strict ban on inductive inference.
